title: Unauthenticated Workload-to-Workload Communication
pattern: Establishing plain-text, unauthenticated socket connections between microservices on internal virtual networks or local cloud environments.
why_bad: Relying on "firewall-only" protection assumes the internal network cannot be bypassed. If an adversary gains a foothold on a single container, they can sniff the unencrypted network wire, capture database credentials, and modify data in transit.
detection: Workload connection methods initiating standard TCP/UDP socket connections without wrapping them in TLS or mutual authenticated RPCs (mTLS).
fix: Use mutually authenticated RPC frameworks (such as gRPC over mTLS or ALTS) to identify and cryptographically secure all workload connections.
source: `Heather Adkins et al. - Building Secure and Reliable Systems (2020)`, Ch 6, p. 104.
